title: Determination of Total Hydrogen Cyanide Levels in Fresh Cassava Roots
author: Matema LE Imakumbili
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.2emgbc6

steps.title: Weigh 100 mg cassava sector
steps.instruction: Place the small plastic balance on its U‑shaped mount (contains a 100 mg weight) or use a 0.0001 g (0.1 mg) digital analytical balance; cut a 1–2 mm thick cross‑section of clean cassava root, remove the peel, cut a sector and trim it until its weight is exactly 100 mg, recording the weight on the balance.

steps.title: Add buffer disc and sample
steps.instruction: In a flat‑bottomed plastic bottle place a round paper disc pre‑impregnated with buffer at pH 6, then place the 100 mg cassava sector on top; do not let the sector stand in air for more than 1 hour before the next step and note the preparation time (samples prepared within 30‑minute intervals should be incubated together).

steps.title: Insert yellow picrate paper
steps.instruction: Immediately add the yellow picrate paper attached to its plastic strip, orienting the longer side of the strip first so the paper stays away from the liquid, and ensure the paper does not touch the liquid.

steps.title: Close bottle with screw lid
steps.instruction: Immediately close the bottle with a screw‑capped lid.

steps.title: Prepare blank and standard controls
steps.instruction: Prepare a blank bottle following the same steps but without any cassava sector; also prepare a control bottle by placing a round disc with a black spot (buffer + enzyme), a pink linamarin standard paper, add 0.5 ml water with a pipette, then add the yellow picrate paper and close immediately.

steps.title: Incubate bottles in dark
steps.instruction: Allow all bottles (samples, blank, standard) to stand for 16–24 h at room temperature in the dark (e.g., inside a cupboard); on cooler days keep for the full 24 h.

steps.title: Dry and label picrate papers
steps.instruction: Open each bottle, carefully remove the picrate papers still attached to their plastic strips, place them on the screw cap or on A4 paper to dry; arrange the 12 papers from one field on the same A4 sheet, label the sheet with the field identifier, and once dry label each paper by placing its identification mark on the plastic strip.

steps.title: Read colour chart
steps.instruction: Compare the colour of the uncovered side of each dried picrate paper with the supplied colour chart and record the cyanide concentration (ppm); verify that the blank reads zero and the standard reads ≈50 ppm; keep the paper on the strip if a later spectrophotometric reading is planned.

steps.title: Store papers for spectrophotometry
steps.instruction: If transport is needed, place each reacted picrate paper in an individual 2 cm × 10 cm plastic bag or wrap in Gladwrap, keep them away from light, store in an opaque container or cool box, ship quickly, and upon arrival place them in a deep freezer; aim to read spectrophotometrically within 1–2 days.

steps.title: Extract picrate into water
steps.instruction: Remove the plastic backing sheet from each dried picrate paper (it can be washed and reused); place the paper in a test tube (or a 25–50 ml beaker) and add exactly 5.0 ml of water measured with a pipette; swirl gently.

steps.title: Stir extraction solution
steps.instruction: Let the tube (or beaker) stand at room temperature for about 30 min with occasional gentle stirring; after 30 min remove the picrate paper with a plastic disposable knife (rinse the knife between samples); the solution should now be colourless.

steps.title: Prepare blank extraction
steps.instruction: Repeat the extraction (steps 10‑11) with the blank picrate paper prepared in step 5, using 5.0 ml water.

steps.title: Measure absorbance at 510 nm
steps.instruction: Set the spectrophotometer to 510 nm, zero it with the blank solution from step 12, then measure the absorbance of each sample solution.

steps.title: Calculate cyanide ppm
steps.instruction: Compute total cyanide (ppm fresh weight) using Equation 1: cyanide (ppm) = 396 × absorbance.

steps.title: Check reproducibility and standards
steps.instruction: Compare the cyanide values obtained from the colour‑chart method (step 8) and the spectrophotometric method (step 13); they should be similar, and the standard should give the expected value.

description: Add 0.5 ml of clean water using the plastic pipette. Notes: Use bottled water for this step if you have no access to distilled water. Tap water may be too variable in composition from one day to the next in some areas. This variability would not be good if you are analysing cyanide in samples over several days.
